hypotheses.justification: Nothing in the statement mentions this instance. `P0` is a `def`, and a def keeps only the section variables its body uses (`removeUnusedVars` in Lean/Elab/MutualDef.lean). Its body `X - X ^ q` needs only `q`, `k` and `[Field k]`, so `P0 q k` elaborates without the instance. The theorem takes it only through the instance-implicit auto-inclusion rule. Mathematically: `k` is algebraically closed of characteristic `q` (`charP_of_galoisField` is just `charP_of_injective_algebraMap' (GaloisField q 2) q`). So `X - X^q` has natDegree `q` (by `one_lt_q`, i.e. `(Fact.out : q.Prime).one_lt`, and `natDegree_sub_eq_right_of_natDegree_lt`), derivative `1`, hence is separable and has `q` distinct roots. None of these steps uses the coordinate ring being a domain. The existing helper lemmas `natDegree_P0`, `derivative_P0` and `separable_P0` carry the instance only as an unused section variable. They can be stated with `omit [IsDomain (CoordRing q k)] in`, or their proofs inlined. The final step (`Multiset.toFinset_card_of_nodup`, `nodup_roots`, `IsAlgClosed.splits`, `natDegree_eq_card_roots`) also needs no such instance.
